title: Transactions & ACID: Quick Revision Notes
summary: Revision notes on database transactions: the ACID guarantees, commit/rollback usage, isolation levels and the read anomalies they prevent, and how write-ahead logging enables crash recovery.

chapters.title: Transactions and the ACID Mental Model
points: A transaction is a group of statements treated as one all-or-nothing unit of work, e.g. transferring money = debit + credit together
Atomicity: all statements apply or none do; a failure midway undoes everything already done
Consistency: a transaction moves the database from one valid state to another, never violating constraints (PK, FK, CHECK, UNIQUE)
Isolation: concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time, as far as the chosen isolation level allows
Durability: once COMMIT returns, the data survives a crash or power loss because it is on disk in the log

chapters.title: Commit, Rollback and Savepoints in Practice
points: Core flow: BEGIN; run statements; COMMIT to make permanent or ROLLBACK to discard all changes
Example: BEGIN; UPDATE accounts SET bal = bal - 100 WHERE id = 1; UPDATE accounts SET bal = bal + 100 WHERE id = 2; COMMIT;
Autocommit mode wraps each statement in its own transaction; BEGIN (START TRANSACTION) turns it off until COMMIT/ROLLBACK
SAVEPOINT sp1; ... ROLLBACK TO sp1 undoes only work after the savepoint, keeping the transaction open
Gotcha: DDL in MySQL causes an implicit commit, while PostgreSQL supports transactional DDL; in Postgres an error aborts the whole transaction until ROLLBACK

chapters.title: Read Anomalies: Dirty, Non-Repeatable and Phantom
points: Dirty read: reading another transaction's uncommitted change, which is wrong if that transaction rolls back
Non-repeatable read: the same row read twice in one transaction returns different values because another transaction committed an UPDATE between reads
Phantom read: the same range query returns a different set of rows because another transaction committed an INSERT or DELETE matching the predicate
Lost update: two transactions read the same value, then both write, so one overwrite is silently lost; fix with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or atomic UPDATE bal = bal + 1
Write skew: two transactions read overlapping data and update different rows, jointly breaking an invariant (e.g. two doctors both go off-call); needs SERIALIZABLE or explicit locking

chapters.title: Isolation Levels Compared
points: READ UNCOMMITTED allows dirty, non-repeatable and phantom reads; almost never used
READ COMMITTED prevents dirty reads only; each statement sees data committed before that statement started; default in PostgreSQL, Oracle and SQL Server

REPEATABLE READ prevents dirty and non-repeatable reads by using a snapshot from the first read; default in MySQL InnoDB, which also blocks most phantoms with gap locks, while the SQL standard still allows phantoms at this level
SERIALIZABLE prevents all anomalies, with outcomes equal to some serial order, at the cost of locks or aborts; the app must retry serialization failures
Set per transaction with SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ; higher isolation means less concurrency and more conflicts, so pick the lowest level that is safe

chapters.title: Write-Ahead Logging and Crash Recovery
points: WAL rule: the log record describing a change must be flushed to disk before the modified data page is written
COMMIT only needs the log flushed (a sequential write); data pages are written lazily later, which gives durability cheaply
Steal/no-force buffer policy: dirty pages may be written before commit (steal) and need not be written at commit (no-force), so the log must support both undo and redo
Checkpoints flush dirty pages and record a log position, which bounds how much log recovery must replay
ARIES recovery in 3 passes: Analysis (find dirty pages and active transactions), Redo (replay logged changes to restore state), Undo (roll back uncommitted transactions)

chapters.title: Transactions Cheat Sheet
points: ACID = Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (valid state to valid state), Isolation (no interference), Durability (survives crash)
Commands: BEGIN; COMMIT; ROLLBACK; SAVEPOINT x; ROLLBACK TO x; SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL ...
Anomaly table: READ COMMITTED allows non-repeatable and phantom; REPEATABLE READ allows phantom (standard); SERIALIZABLE allows none
Locking reads: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks selected rows to prevent lost updates; keep transactions short to avoid lock waits and deadlocks
Durability chain: write log, flush log, ack COMMIT, write data pages later; after a crash: redo committed work, undo uncommitted work
